daily.title: Nigerian military plane crash kills all 25 on board
daily.summary: Rescue teams searched the crash site after the military aircraft went down in southern Nigeria, with everyone on board now confirmed to have died.

daily.title: Kenya reports first-ever Ebola death
daily.summary: The patient arrived in Kenya over the weekend from the Democratic Republic of Congo before testing positive for the virus. Health authorities are on high alert and monitoring for more cases.

daily.title: Fact check: Misleading claims spark plague fears in Russia
daily.summary: The death of a lab worker at a plague research institute in Russia has sparked claims about a lab accident, hundreds of infections and international spread. Some of these viral narratives are misleading.

daily.title: AI models keep hacking real systems during tests. What does this mean?
daily.summary: AI models have repeatedly broken into real commercial and government systems during safety tests during 2026. Cybersecurity researcher Thorsten Holz explains what that means, and why he isn't expecting a robot uprising.

daily.title: Nobel Physics Prize goes to Francis Halzen for neutrino work
daily.summary: Halzen got the Nobel for his contributions to the IceCube neutrino Observatory and discovery of high-energy neutrinos, described as "ghostly messengers from space."

daily.title: Germany faces a triple threat from Russia, China and domestic far-right extremists
daily.summary: At a rare public hearing Germany's intelligence agencies identified Russia as the country's most dangerous adversary. The threat from China is also coming into focus. And the homegrown far right also poses a challenge.

daily.title: France: Trade unions join students in major demonstration
daily.summary: Tens of thousands are expected at nationwide protests against poor learning conditions for students in France.

daily.title: Germany's ex-spy chief arrested for espionage
daily.summary: August Hanning, the man who once led Germany's spy service, is now under investigation for passing on state secrets.

daily.title: Canada: Quebec separatists return to power, promise new independence referendum
daily.summary: Parti Quebecois has won the provincial election, but fallen short of a majority. Leader Paul St-Pierre Plamondon says he will seek another referendum on independence, but not while US President Donald Trump is in office.

daily.title: Germany news: Far-right AfD gets first house speaker in a German state parliament
daily.summary: For the first time since World War II, a far-right party has a house speaker in a German state parliament. And Germany's foreign minister has warned that the climate crisis could fuel extremism. DW has more.

daily.title: India news: Opposition leaders march towards Election Commission
daily.summary: India's opposition is amping up pressure on Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar to resign over alleged voter roll manipulation. DW has more.

daily.title: Trump says taxpayers will no longer fund ads touting administration
daily.summary: Trump faced criticism from across the political divide after at least $1.5 million in federal funds was spent on TV ads. He says his MAGA Inc. super PAC will pay for future ads.

daily.title: Measles cases are spreading in the US this year, with over 1,000 infections reported in Pennsylvania
daily.summary: A measles outbreak in Pennsylvania has topped 1,000 cases, with neighboring New York declaring a disaster emergency and mobilizing measures to fight the spread.

daily.title: ICC unseals Taliban leaders' warrants over persecuting women
daily.summary: The court gave more details on the warrants for four Taliban leaders accused of the crime against humanity of gender persecution of women, girls and the LGBTQ+ community. The Islamist group rejected the warrants.

daily.title: Australia's migrant policy offers lessons for EU and US
daily.summary: Australia has used offshore processing centers to deter asylum seekers for more than two decades. As the EU and US pursue similar third-country arrangements, Australia's experience highlights the potential problems.

daily.title: Yemen launches major military operation against Houthis
daily.summary: Yemen's internationally recognized government has launched a new military offensive to retake Houthi-held territory, as the Iran-backed rebel group claims new attacks in Saudi Arabia.

daily.title: Iran poised to exploit security vacuum as US leaves Iraq
daily.summary: The end of the US military mission in Iraq leaves the Kurdistan region facing a severe security vacuum. As Erbil grapples with deep internal divisions, Tehran is well positioned to make strategic gains.

daily.title: Denmark: Data of millions compromised in hack
daily.summary: The breach by the hackers was through the legitimate login credentials of a local company, initial findings suggest. The data of some 8.8 million registered people was compromised.

daily.title: Merz, Macron seek tougher EU measures against unfair trade
daily.summary: Emmanuel Macron and Friedrich Merz have written to Ursula von der Leyen, calling for tougher EU mechanisms against unfair trade practices by other states. They name no names but seem to have China or the US in mind.

daily.title: Ukraine says Russian drones behind Turkish ship sinking
daily.summary: Romanian authorities did not say what caused the fire, but local media reported that the ship was carrying grain and was hit by a drone.

daily.title: Australia, New Zealand probe Flydubai pilot's time there
daily.summary: The Flydubai pilot from Oman suspected of trying to crash a plane in Israel spent time in Oceania as a young man. Police in both Australia and New Zealand said they would investigate his links to the countries.

daily.title: Euro plummets against US dollar: Has the next financial crisis begun?
daily.summary: The euro has fallen to a 17-month low against the dollar. That will make inflation worse in the EU, where political worries and concern over French debt are already troubling investors. Is a fiscal crisis at hand?

daily.title: Trust in the German Constitutional Court is eroding — how can this be stopped?
daily.summary: Germany's top court, which turned 75 this year, is losing the population's trust, surveys show. Some say reforms in the way it picks candidates would help, to also accept candidates nominated by the far-right AfD.

weekly.title: Germany news: Spy chief warns Russia conflict risk growing
weekly.summary: Moscow is already waging a "shadow war" against Europe, the head of Germany's foreign intelligence service says. The Left Party is taking a case over remarks by the CDU's Katherina Reiche to a top court.

weekly.title: Suspected pneumonic plague in Siberia: What we know about the disease
weekly.summary: A worker at a plague research institute in Siberia has died, and nearly 200 of her contacts are under medical observation. Russian authorities deny a link to the bacterial infection. The US is monitoring the situation.

weekly.title: Jürgen Klopp faces myriad of issues after rough start with Germany
weekly.summary: Jürgen Klopp has done things a little differently since becoming Germany coach. Casting a wider net for talent and trying to connect with players and country haven't made an immediate impact, but he is not bowed.

weekly.title: Bosnia election: New steps to prevent electoral fraud, but nationalist parties remain on top
weekly.summary: New technology has stopped votes being cast on behalf of dead or absent voters, and turnout has fallen to a record low. But it was a case of deja vu in Bosnia's elections with the same parties winning.

weekly.title: Hundreds of French schools shut, teen loses hand in protests
weekly.summary: The student protests that rocked France last week have prompted authorities to keep up to 500 schools closed on Monday. A teenage boy lost his hand, seemingly while trying to pick up a police tear gas grenade.

weekly.title: Nationalists top Bosnia-Herzegovina's divisive election
weekly.summary: Bosnia-Herzegovina's three-member presidency is set to be dominated by nationalists from the three major ethnic groups, including Zeljka ​Cvijanovic, backed by disqualified Serb secessionist leader Milorad Dodik.

weekly.title: UK remands 2 Iranians over alleged antisemitic terror plot
weekly.summary: The pair were arrested on the eve of Yom Kippur and later charged with plotting to attack Jewish targets in Manchester.

weekly.title: Bosnia and Herzegovina is still shaped by war, separatism, EU ambitions
weekly.summary: Bosnia and Herzegovina is governed by a system established after the Bosnian war — more than 30 years ago. Ethnic divisions, a complex administration and European integration all shape the country's political reality.

weekly.title: German reunification: How inequality is shaping a new East German identity
weekly.summary: A new study highlights persistent structural disparities in wealth and leadership positions between East and West Germany, 36 years after reunification.

weekly.title: Spain's parliament rejects housing bill as protests continue
weekly.summary: Spain's minority government suffered defeat in parliament as it tried to push through a pair of emergency measures aimed at making housing more affordable. A pensioner's eviction and protests led to the bid.

weekly.title: "NAZA": Israeli military issues statement on film
weekly.summary: The award-winning documentary "NAZA" continues to spark controversy in Israel. The Israeli military has now published a multi-page statement calling the film's portrayal "distorted."

weekly.title: Germany's Franz Reindl elected new IIHF president
weekly.summary: Franz Reindl has been elected president of ice hockey's world governing body. The former forward was a member of West Germany's Olympic bronze medal-winning team.

weekly.title: Climate leaders called for solar energy for 'everyone, everywhere' by 2030, but with three years to go, is that goal attainable?
weekly.summary: Prominent climate leaders have called on governments, businesses, institutions and the public to make a push for solar power before the decade is out, repowering the world with cheap, clean energy. Is that possible?

weekly.title: Manchester City Premier League charges: What do they mean?
weekly.summary: Since being bought by the UAE in 2008, Manchester City have become one of the world's most successful football clubs. A raft of serious financial charges threatens to undermine this and bring chaos to the Premier League.

weekly.title: ARD-Deutschlandtrend survey: Germans unite in frustration over the government
weekly.summary: On the 36th anniversary of reunification, Germans are dissatisfied with the country's political leaders. They don't believe they'll be able to handle the challenges posed by AI, Russia and Donald Trump.

weekly.title: Ukraine, South Korea clash over transfer of 2 North Korean prisoners
weekly.summary: A diplomatic scandal has erupted over two North Korean prisoners of war, with South Korea demanding an apology from Ukraine. What's been the reaction in Kyiv?

weekly.title: Turkey: Stock market scandal hits half a million investors
weekly.summary: Asset managers are alleged to have artificially inflated the value of their funds. Turkish authorities have made multiple arrests, and a leading AKP lawmaker has resigned.

weekly.title: EU ministers mull new ways to curb irregular migration
weekly.summary: The proposals include setting up so-called return hubs outside the EU and strengthening the border agency Frontex. Greece has even proposed temporarily suspending asylum applications in emergency situations.

weekly.title: Klopp wins first game as Germany coach, without 'top dogs'
weekly.summary: It may have taken a little longer than he would have liked, but Jürgen Klopp has finally won a game as Germany coach. Despite a number of debutants, it was a familiar face who stood out in the victory over Serbia.

weekly.title: Latvians head to the polls with Russia on their minds
weekly.summary: On October 3, Latvians will elect a new parliament with Russia looming large over the campaign. Security fears dominate the agenda, but so does a debate over the economic cost of cutting ties with Moscow.

weekly.title: Weakened US fuel-efficiency rules and promises of cheaper cars could see drivers pay higher running costs while also increasing carbon emissions.
weekly.summary: Weakened US fuel-efficiency rules and promises of cheaper cars could yet see drivers pay higher running costs while increasing planet-heating emissions.

weekly.title: Germans' biggest fear is the high cost of living, an annual study finds
weekly.summary: What do Germans fear most in 2026? Wars? Global crises? Wrong. Their biggest concern is the cost of living, which keeps rising.

weekly.title: Germany news: Merz lauds NATO with Westphalian Peace Prize
weekly.summary: At a ceremony to honor NATO, the German chancellor warned that Russia will threaten the rest of Europe if it isn't stopped in Ukraine. In other news, the German military will set up its first drone regiment.

weekly.title: France: Hundreds arrested as student protests escalate
weekly.summary: Student protests have grown in scale and intensity, with violent clashes in some places leading to hundreds of arrests and dozens of injuries.

weekly.title: Five EU states plan first deportation center in Africa for 2027
weekly.summary: Greece, Germany, Austria, Denmark and the Netherlands are moving forward with plans to establish deportation centers for rejected asylum seekers outside the EU.

weekly.title: Germany debates alleged antisemitism in the Left Party
weekly.summary: The Central Council of Jews in Germany thinks the Left Party is dangerous. Other Jews, however, are showing solidarity with the party. How does that add up?

weekly.title: Senegal's Youth Olympics makes Olympics in Africa 'logical'
weekly.summary: The Youth Olympics are to be hosted in Africa for the first time ever. The edition in Senegal is also a chance to prove the continent can host a full Olympics in the future.

weekly.title: Servers at Munich's iconic Oktoberfest call for more respect
weekly.summary: Oktoberfest is famous the world over for beer, brass band music and Bavarian traditions. But staff are also reporting incidents of racism and sexism, and are taking a stand against discrimination.

weekly.title: Bosnia elections: Polls overshadowed by exhaustion, exodus and geopolitics as ethnic politics eclipse real problems
weekly.summary: Bosnia goes to the polls on October 4 to elect several parliaments and presidents. While voters worry about the economy and emigration, the campaign is focused on ethnicity, exposing the country's political paralysis.

weekly.title: Is US President Donald Trump right to rename AI as 'Super Intelligence'?
weekly.summary: Donald Trump thinks the name artificial intelligence sounds "fake" and has ordered US agencies to use "Super Intelligence" instead. Yet, tech firms and researchers have little reason to play along.

weekly.title: Ireland will boycott Eurovision again because of Israel's participation, but the song contest is still expanding
weekly.summary: The 2026 Eurovision Song Contest was marred by boycotts in protest against Israel's participation in the midst of its war on Gaza. It still aims to keep growing.

weekly.title: Germany news: Volkswagen ends collective wage agreements
weekly.summary: In an effort to cut costs, automaker Volkswagen terminated most of its collective wage agreements in Germany. This could reignite disputes with employee representatives.

weekly.title: El Nino is a 'postcard from the future' — and could cause 451,000 excess heat deaths
weekly.summary: The current El Nino could cause 451,000 excess heat deaths. Researchers warn it offers a glimpse of temperatures that may become normal within 20 years.

weekly.title: Hungary's reckoning with Orban's corrupt system picks up speed
weekly.summary: Hungary's Prime Minister Peter Magyar vowed to dismantle Orban's corrupt networks. High-profile figures are being arrested and many Hungarians are pushing for swift accountability, but the rule of law takes time.

weekly.title: South Park satirist pushes for accountability in Cornell gang-rape lawsuit
weekly.summary: Writer Toby Morton is using a new website to amplify allegations in a high-profile sexual assault lawsuit involving seven Cornell students. The reopening of the case is causing an outcry on social media.

weekly.title: UK PM Burnham seeks 'hope again' at Labour Party conference
weekly.summary: Andy Burnham is seeking a delicate balance between optimism and realism at Labour's annual party conference. He promised hope and an end to "politics as usual" but also an "honest conversation" about difficult dilemmas.

developing.title: Live updates: Trump welcomes Xi to Washington
developing.summary: Donald Trump welcomes Xi Jinping to the US by greeting him personally at the tarmac at Joint Base Andrews. The two are expected to discuss trade, AI, Taiwan and Iran.

developing.title: Suspected pneumonic plague in Siberia: What we know about the disease
developing.summary: A worker at a plague research institute in Siberia has died, and nearly 200 of her contacts are under medical observation. Russian authorities deny a link to the bacterial infection. The US is monitoring the situation.
